title: Imaging of ultrasound specularity at cortical bone interfaces to detect unbalanced remodeling: A preliminary study
authors: Amadou S. Dia; Salomé Vignat; Guillaume Renaud; Quentin Grimal
matched_query: ultrasound specularity imaging cortical bone remodeling beamforming refraction
reasons: direct ultrasound image reconstruction and quantitative biomarker mapping
journal metadata and DOI cross-checked against the arXiv journal reference
summary_en: Reconstructs cortical-bone endosteal specularity maps by combining specular-reflector enhancement with refraction-aware beamforming. Numerical and ex vivo experiments show a strong association between reduced specularity and enlarged pores or surface roughness linked to unbalanced bone remodeling.

summary_en: An adjoint-based distributed source inversion method that reconstructs effective spatiotemporal ultrasound-transducer models from measured wavefields. The calibrated sources improve directivity and waveform reproduction and substantially improve reverse-time-migration and full-waveform-inversion reconstructions.

summary_en: Derives a wave-based forward model and inverse Stolt mapping for 3-D plane-wave imaging with row–column addressed arrays. Angular spectrum completion and conjugate cross-correlation compounding improve image quality, while FFT-domain reconstruction is reported to be about 231 times faster than delay-and-sum for a 256×256×512 volume.

summary_en: Introduces Hadamard-encoded full-aperture transmissions and synthetic beamforming for high-frame-rate acoustoelectric current-source imaging. Using 16 transmit events, the system images single and distributed dipole sources at 500 Hz and reports about a 5 dB SNR improvement over focused-beam scanning after pressure equalization.
